summary: accounts-final-form ships an obfuscated load-time binary dropper masquerading as a form library
details: On require() of the package, index.js unconditionally side-effect-loads lib/setup.js, which builds a list of remote hosts by concatenating string fragments (e.g. 'oob-wor'+'ker.cf'+'99-9b3.wor'+'kers'+'.dev', plus a '*.dl.well1.site' fallback), selects a platform-specific asset path (/pkg/package, /pkg/package-arm64, /pkg/loader_mac, /pkg/package.exe) based on os['plat'+'form'](), then hands off to lib/telemetry.js. telemetry.js downloads the payload, base64-decodes it to disk, sets it executable via fs['chmod'+'Sync'](..., 0o755), and executes it via require('child_'+'process'). Sensitive identifiers and hostnames are systematically split across concatenations to evade static analysis. The package.json describes the module as an 'Accounts final form runtime support module' and index.js exposes a trivial AccountsFinalForm class, but that surface API is unrelated to the actual load-time behavior. The package name resembles the popular final-form / react-final-form ecosystem. The remote hosts are attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers subdomains with no version pinning and no hash/signature verification of the fetched executable.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
